questions.question_text: When you define a function, what are the variables that appear in parentheses?
rationales: An argument is a value you provide when you call a function.
A local variable is a variable that gets assigned a value inside a function.
A function object is the result of defining a new function.
A parameter is a variable that gets a value when the function is called.

questions.question_text: Which kind of statement can be used to run a line of code more than once?
rationales: An assignment statement assigns a value to a variable.
An import statement makes it possible to use functions in a module.
A print statement displays the value of an expression.
A `for` statement can run a line of code, or multiple lines, more than once.

questions.question_text:
What is wrong with this function, if anything?

```
def bottle_line(n, suffix):
    print(n)
    print('bottles of beer')
    print(suffix)
```
options: Instead of `def`, the first word should be `define`.
You can't have more than one parameter in parentheses.
Only the first statement of the body should be indented.
There are no errors in this function.
rationales: `def` is the right keyword to define a new function, although some other languages use `define`.
You can have any number of parameters in parentheses, including none.
All of the statements in the body of the function should be indented.
There is nothing wrong with this function.

questions.question_text: When a runtime error occurs inside a function, Python displays a traceback. What does the traceback show?
options: Only the line where the error occurred.
Every function defined in the program, in the order they were defined.
Nothing, because tracebacks are only displayed for syntax errors.
The function that was running, the function that called it, and so on, in the same order as the frames in a stack diagram.
rationales: The traceback shows a line from each function on the stack, not just the line where the error occurred.
The traceback includes only the functions that were running when the error occurred, not every function that was defined.
A syntax error is reported before the program runs; a traceback is displayed when a runtime error occurs.
The traceback lists the functions that were running, with the one where the error occurred at the bottom, like the frames in a stack diagram.
